facts.statement: The extinct animal belongs to the genus Eocoracias.
The only known species within this genus is Eocoracias brachyptera.
The genus was described by Mayr and Mourer-Chauviré in 2000.
Eocoracias is classified within the parent group Coracii.
Eocoracias brachyptera lived approximately 47 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Eocoracias brachyptera, and it lived approximately 47 million years ago (Lutetian stage) based on dating of the fossil site.

facts.statement: The genus existed between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Lutetian (48.07 to 41.03 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Eocoracias have been discovered at the Messel Pit in Germany.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found at the Messel Pit in Germany.

facts.statement: A specimen of Eocoracias is notable for preserving non-iridescent structural coloration on its feathers, a feature previously unknown in fossil birds.
facts.quote: It is known for a specimen having preserved non-iridescent structural coloration on its feathers, previously unknown in fossil birds.

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Eocoracias.

rejected.statement: This animal is classified as a bird (Class Aves).
Eocoracias is an extinct bird related to modern rollers and other Coraciiformes like kingfishers and bee-eaters.
rejected.quote: Eocoracias is an extinct genus of bird related to modern rollers and other Coraciiformes such as kingfishers, bee-eaters, motmots, and todies.
